Attempt 4 (current best): moved the particle table to an extern global (Data_0203cd00[1024], address unresolved/placeholder) instead of a stack local, since the reference's 64-byte frame proves the table cannot be a local. class improved to structural-topology, wrong_instructions=625, differing_halfwords=679. bl call targets for both Func_080e0524 calls and the Func_08002f40/Func_080072f0 setup now match the reference's targets exactly (visible in candidate-show diff as unmarked lines), confirming that call-graph recovery. The remaining divergence starts at the prologue itself: the reference holds four values live across the whole function in r8/r9/r10/r11 (mov r7,fp; mov r6,sl; mov r5,r9; push {r5,r6,r7}; mov r7,r8; push {r7}), but the current draft's reduced local set (no y_offset/record_slot/screen/record locals, and a simplified frame-loop body that is mostly stubbed placeholder logic) only pressures two callee-saved registers, so GCC allocates a visibly different, shorter prologue and the whole instruction stream shifts out of alignment from there.
attempt_9: Mapped every `ldr r,[pc,#N]` in games/gs1/asm/080d4ce8.s whose target lands past the retained object's own text end (0x36a) onto the 16-word ROM gap list from attempt_7, by assembling the region standalone (arm-none-eabi-as + arm-none-eabi-objdump -d --disassemble-zeroes -Mforce-thumb out/gs1-en/asm/080d4ce8.o) and reading each instruction's own comment-annotated local target address (e.g. `@ (0x36c ...)`), then adding 0x080d4ce8 to get the real address and indexing into the attempt_7 word list (0x36c=w0 ... 0x3a8=w15, 16 consecutive words, one per 4 bytes -- confirms the whole gap is this region's own tail literal pool with no slack). This produced several confirmed, evidence-backed corrections applied to the .c: (1) `efx->unk1C` was wrong in every one of its 5 uses -- the real field read is offset 24 (0x18), which is the struct's existing `layers` member, not `unk1C` (offset 28); replaced throughout. (2) The anchor-init bias table and the per-frame draw-loop cell table were both wrongly aliased to one invented symbol `Data_080ede9f`; the real pool values are two distinct, already-plausible addresses -- 0x080ee29d (anchor bias, ldrsb i.e. **signed** byte, indexed by `layers*4+i`) and 0x080ee2a9 (draw-loop cell table, matches the already-declared-but-misused `Data_080ee2a9`) -- split into `Data_080ee29d` (new, s8) and reused `Data_080ee2a9` correctly. (3) rectangle[46]/[47] and the per-frame canvas-like pointer were read from the wrong heap-cache window: this owner reads them from `Data_03001e50[46]`/`[47]`/`[12]` (the corpus-wide 'Data_03001e50[kind] holds kind's block address' cache already established in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080cc5d8.c, 080dd2c4.c, 080e7404.c, 080ceff8.c), not from `Data_03001eec[46]`/`[47]`/`[1]` as the draft had it -- 0x03001e80 (the dossier's previously-unattributed 'second heap-cache pointer') is exactly Data_03001e50[12] ((0x03001e80-0x03001e50)/4=12), and it is re-read every frame at the real loop-reentry address (sub_080d4e4c = local offset 0x164), not reused from the startup Data_03001eec[1] read. (4) The particle-spawn magnitude/angle were built from the wrong inputs: real code is `magnitude = rand()&0x3ff` (not `Data_080ee2a9[0]&rand()`) and `angle = (rand()&0x7fff) + 0xffffc000` (not `magnitude+rand()`), with the `+32` magnitude bump happening after the cosine call per the real instruction order -- spelled with the exact masks read from the gap pool (w13=0x3ff, w14=0x7fff, w15=0xffffc000) per this round's lead (1). Net effect on candidate-show: matched_prefix stays capped at 7 and differing_halfwords moved from 650 to 661 (candidate_bytes 1212->1244, sub sp #64->#84) -- confirms attempt 4's finding that the front-of-function ldmia/frame-size mismatch (not yet fixed) dominates and cascades into every later offset comparison, so this round's corrections are real, evidence-backed structural fixes but are not yet visible in the score. They should be kept regardless: reverting to the old wrong offsets/masks to chase a marginally lower cosmetic diff under a known-broken prefix would trade correctness for a meaningless number.
attempt_10: Ran the frame-ledger technique per next_steps (lens.ts had never actually been run against this owner before -- only the guess-and-recompile loop had). (1) Enumerated every [sp,#N] access across both retained-asm files: distinct offsets 0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,40,44,52,56 (part 2's set -- 0,4,8,12,24,28,32,36,40 -- is the same physical frame, no new offsets). 14 word slots = 56 bytes inside the reference's `sub sp, #64`; offsets 48 and 60 are never touched by ldr/str/add in either file, i.e. two 4-byte slots the reference reserves but never re-reads -- the same 'declared array/local with zero accesses' signature the walker dossier used to explain a GCC 2.96 frame-size gap. (2) Enumerated every r8-r11 touch: r11 (fp) is set once near the very top (`mov fp, r1` from the ldmia's first word) and then referenced via `add rX, fp` at at least 9 separate sites scattered across the whole function body in both files -- a single long-lived base-address pseudo, matching `work` (heap[0]) in the current draft, which is already declared first and used throughout. r8/r9/r10 are each reused for 3-4 unrelated short-lived values at different points (mov r8,r3 / mov r8,r0 / mov r8,r7, etc.) rather than one variable living the whole function -- so only fp/r11 is a true whole-function aggregate pointer; r8-r10 are just what the allocator promoted into hard high registers under heap-cache-window register pressure, not named locals with special lifetime shape. (3) Ran `bun tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts 080d4ce8` against the current (attempt_9) source for the first time: all 286 pseudos in the emitted order show LO_REGS or BASE_REGS as their only preferred class -- none show a HI_REGS preference or an r8-r11 hard assignment anywhere in the dump. This is the actual mechanical reason matched_prefix is stuck at 7: the current draft's simultaneous-live-value count under LO_REGS (r0-r7) never rises high enough, at any point in the function, for global.c to spill a pseudo into r8-r11 the way the reference does -- so the prologue difference (2 registers / 64-byte frame vs 4 registers / 88-byte frame) is a real, measured register-pressure gap, not a frame-size cosmetic. (4) Baseline rescore reproduces attempt_9 exactly: candidate=1244 reference=1360, differing_halfwords=661, class=structural-topology, matched_prefix=7, candidate frame is `sub sp, #84` (not yet 64 or 88 either). No source edit was applied this round: per attempt_8/attempt_9's own finding, changing the heap-read spelling alone does not move the register-pressure needle (confirmed again structurally via lens.ts, not just by recompiling), and no candidate edit was found this round that visibly raised any pseudo's live-range overlap enough to trigger an r8-r11 assignment in the lens output, so nothing was committed that would trade a verified-correct structural fix for an unverified cosmetic diff shift, per attempt_9's own caution.
